review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve explicit settings in independently supplied environments**

After default process-wide seeding, an independently constructed `env` containing `HF_XET_FIXED_DOWNLOAD_CONCURRENCY="128"` and explicit `HF_XET_CLIENT_AC_MIN_DOWNLOAD_CONCURRENCY="1"` loses its MIN setting here, even with `force=False`, because it matches the parent seed. `_SEEDED_INTO_ENVIRON` only records writes to `os.environ`; this separate mapping was never seeded by Zoo. Deleting its explicit primary lets the alias change the requested minimum from 1 to 128. The added explicit-primary tests likewise fail after seeding a 32-core/128-GB profile, where the parent's MAX seed matches their explicit value of 64. Limit cleanup to targets known to contain inherited seeds rather than treating value equality as ownership across arbitrary mappings.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Fixed in e392cc47: seeded AC values are now cleared only from os.environ, where ownership is known; child envs are already cleaned by resize_for_cache_dir, and a caller-built mapping keeps its explicit primaries (new regression test).

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clear seed ownership when removing a generated AC value**

After this cleanup runs once, a subsequent explicit primary can still be deleted because `_SEEDED_INTO_ENVIRON` retains the removed entry. For example, seed defaults, set `HF_XET_FIXED_DOWNLOAD_CONCURRENCY=128`, apply to clear the seeds, then explicitly set `HF_XET_CLIENT_AC_MIN_DOWNLOAD_CONCURRENCY=1` and apply again: the last call deletes that new user setting even with `force=False`, allowing the alias to change the minimum to 128. This is reproducible in `os.environ` despite the caller-mapping fix. Clear the corresponding ownership record when removing a seed so later explicit assignments are preserved.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
Fixed in 19f86533: clearing a seeded AC value now drops its ownership record too, so a primary set afterwards is kept (new regression test).

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retire AC seed ownership when resizing the real environment**

Under a newly enabled fixed alias, `resize_for_cache_dir(os.environ, ...)` removes seeded AC variables before entering this loop but retains their `_SEEDED_INTO_ENVIRON` records. Because `target.get(key)` is already `None`, this cleanup never retires those records. Unlike the now-fixed direct-apply sequence, the resize-then-apply sequence still reproduces the problem: explicitly setting `HF_XET_CLIENT_AC_MIN_DOWNLOAD_CONCURRENCY="1"` after resizing and calling `apply_xet_env()` again deletes that user setting, allowing a fixed alias of 128 to win. Clear ownership when the resize removes real-environment seeds as well.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Fixed in 568285af: resize_for_cache_dir now retires the record of every seed it clears from os.environ, so a seed record always means our value is live there; the following apply re-records what it writes (new regression test).

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Propagate removed AC keys into the download spawn environment**

When the fixed alias is enabled after import-time seeding, `_run_download_attempt` (`unsloth_zoo_downloads/hf_xet_fallback.py:2023`) calls `resize_for_cache_dir(dict(os.environ), ...)` and overlays only its returned writes before spawning. Removing the AC entries here means the deletions in that temporary mapping never reach the actual spawn environment, so the child retains the parent's generated primaries and still ignores the alias. This also newly bypasses cache-directory concurrency resizing: in a mocked-spawn reproduction, the child's ceiling stays at the parent's 124 instead of the destination-sized 14 returned before this change. Propagate removals through the spawn/restore path and add a regression that inspects the environment at `proc.start()`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
Fixed in 1d352312: the spawn window now also removes every seed the resize dropped from its copy without rewriting, and restores it afterwards; regression test inspects the env at proc.start().
